stories.headline: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Sets Rotten Tomatoes Audience Score Records - Forbes
stories.why: This isn't just nostalgia—it signals that '90s-era supernatural romance is resonating with audiences tired of cynical reboots, validating a specific emotional register (female agency, magic as metaphor) that's been absent from mainstream fantasy.

stories.headline: Jay Maisel, a cigar-chomping giant of photography, has died - The Washington Post
stories.summary: He photographed Marilyn Monroe and took the cover photo for Miles Davis’s “Kind of Blue.” For 50 years, he lived in a vast graffiti-covered bank building.
stories.why: Maisel defined the visual language of cool for decades; his death marks the end of an era when a photographer could be as famous as the celebrities they shot, and when living like an artist (literally in a graffiti building) was culturally celebrated rather than gentrified.

stories.headline: NYT Connections hints and answers for September 12. Tips to solve 'Connections' #1189. - Mashable
stories.why: This daily puzzle has become a status game for the 25-45 male demographic—solving it faster than colleagues signals intelligence without the pretension of wordle, making it the preferred office/group chat flex.

stories.headline: Woman Dead After Undergoing 6 Cosmetic Procedures at Once - TMZ
stories.summary: A woman who underwent 6 cosmetic procedures at once during a marathon 8-hour procedure has died ... and now the 51-year-old's sister is demanding answers.
stories.why: This tragedy exposes the cosmetic surgery industrial complex targeting women with unrealistic timelines; for men, it's a reminder of how normalized extreme body modification has become among partners/friends, raising uncomfortable questions about pressure and risk tolerance.

stories.headline: I saw the movie that Warner tried to delete: 'Coyote vs. Acme' - Fox Business
stories.summary: "Coyote vs. Acme's" story parallels one of how the movie fought through Warner Bros. and tax incentives and got to movie theaters nationwide.
stories.why: A studio trying to bury a mid-budget film that actually got released is rare enough to matter—it signals both the desperation of legacy studios and a shift where grassroots support can override corporate erasure.

stories.headline: The Family Stone Sequel In Works With Almost All Cast Returning - Deadline
stories.summary: 'The Family Stone' is getting a sequel from Searchlight, with Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker and more returning.
stories.why: A 'Family Stone' sequel works because that 2005 film created a specific template for modern family dysfunction that later holiday movies mimicked; this is Hollywood admitting that specific formula still hits, especially as this demographic navigates their own fraught family dynamics.

stories.headline: Insomniac Explains Wolverine’s Already-Infamous ‘Fart Gas Trails’ - Forbes
stories.why: Insomniac defending a ridiculous detail (fart physics in a $200M+ game) shows how seriously AAA developers now engage with online criticism—it's a microcosm of how gamer feedback shapes design in ways that matter to players who've grown up expecting customization and explanation.

stories.headline: 'A legend': Celine Dion poised for emotional comeback in Paris - yahoo.com
stories.summary: Celine Dion was on Saturday set to make her long-awaited return to the stage in Paris after years battling a rare neurological disorder, with anticipation am...
stories.why: Dion's return after Stiff-Person Syndrome isn't just a comeback—it's a cultural reset moment proving that physical limitation doesn't erase talent, which matters to men watching their own bodies betray them or aging out of invulnerability.
